candidates.title: Subway co-founder's relative bought $6.75m warehouse; plans $1.8m revamp
candidates.excerpt: A member of the Buck family has purchased a Danbury warehouse previously owned by the Salame family. This transaction, completed for $6.75 million, signals a commitment to modernizing the site while preserving its industrial purpose. Plans include extensive renovations and the construction of an office building alongside the warehouse. The investment reflects confidence in the local economy and aims to maintain vibrant commercial use of the property.

candidates.title: Delhi protests India’s internal matter, won’t comment: Marco Rubio
candidates.excerpt: On Tuesday, more than 20 UN human rights experts in Geneva had expressed alarm over what they described as a “repeatedly heavy-handed police response” to peaceful youth-led demonstrations in the national capital. United States secretary of state Marco Rubio brushed aside criticism by “UN experts” of the Indian crackdown as he called them an “oxymoron”.

candidates.title: Who are the terrorists? J&K and Ladakh high court questions ‘vague’ detention order
candidates.excerpt: A single bench of Justice Wasim Nargal said preventive detention, which allows authorities to deprive a person of liberty without a regular criminal trial, demands the “highest degree of constitutional responsibility and procedural diligence”. The court directed the DC to appear with the detention order, police dossier, material placed before him and records showing his consideration of the case and subjective satisfaction before ordering detention under PSA.

candidates.title: AI-generated Vidhana Soudha blast clip lands Bihar native in police net
candidates.excerpt: A 25-year-old man from Bihar has been arrested in Bengaluru for allegedly uploading an AI-generated video falsely showing an explosion at Vidhana Soudha. Police registered a case at Vidhana Soudha police station and are investigating the matter.
